exposure: Exposure to tobacco smoke during pregnancy
cohort: 200 pregnant women near the end of their pregnancies, divided into a group of smokers and a group of non-smokers, studied in Iraq in 2023.
finding: Maternal smoking during pregnancy was associated with higher rates of cesarean sections, preeclampsia, and differences in birth weight and gestational age, with smokers having smaller and earlier babies.
mod_finding: 71% of women who smoked had cesarean sections compared to 44% of women who did not smoke.
cross-section timing: Around the end of pregnancy in 2023
birth_weight: Differences in birth weight were observed between groups (smokers had smaller babies).
gest_age: Differences in gestational age at birth were observed between groups (smokers had earlier babies).
